transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. It's really nice to meet you, and thank you for taking the time to see me. 

Um... well, I guess what brings me in is... I've always been a pretty energetic guy, which is usually a good thing, right? But lately, I feel like I’m just always moving from one thing to the next. Like I just can’t really sit idle. And, um, we recently got a new work setup—I do customer service—and it’s just made it a lot harder to sort of... hide it, I guess? 

I hope that makes sense. It's nothing terrible, really, I just want to make sure I'm doing what I need to do to be a good employee, so I thought it would be best to get it checked out. Is that an okay reason to come in?
Have you had any distinct periods where you felt unusually energized or overactive compared with your normal self?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've always been an energetic guy, like I said, but it's just kind of a constant thing. It's not like I have these sudden bursts where I'm bouncing off the walls or anything crazy like that. It's just my normal, everyday self, you know? I'm just a little restless sometimes. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for. I'm not trying to be difficult, I just really don't think I've ever had a time where I felt way more energized than usual. Is that okay?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot more days than not?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I care about doing a good job, of course, and making sure my customers are happy, but I don't really sit around stressing or worrying about things most days. I try to keep a pretty positive attitude, actually. 

I hope that's a good thing? I just don't want you to think I'm, like, a nervous wreck or anything. It's really just the restlessness I mentioned. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering these right for you.
Did these restlessness and attention problems begin before age 12?

Well, um... yeah, I guess so. I mean, it’s not just the new work setup. Looking back, I suppose I’ve kind of always been this way? Like, even way back in grade school, I remember my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright—which was nice of them to say!—but they’d also put down that I was a little careless sometimes, or that I talked out of turn. 

They always had to remind me to stay focused on my work. But, you know, I was just a kid, and kids are naturally a bit squirmy, right? I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad student or a troublemaker. I always meant well! I just... had a hard time staying on track, I guess. Is that the kind of thing you meant?
Do you usually avoid social or work situations because you’re afraid of being judged, criticized, or embarrassed?

Oh, no, no, definitely not. I actually really enjoy being around people. That's part of why I like my job in customer service, you know? I get to talk to folks all day. I don't really get embarrassed or worry about people judging me. I just try to be friendly and helpful. 

I hope that's alright? I mean, I know I can be a little chatty sometimes, like I said about school, but I never try to hide away from people or anything like that. I like to think I'm a pretty outgoing guy. Does that sound okay to you?
Do you often interrupt people or blurt out answers before they’ve finished asking a question?

Well, um... maybe a little bit? I really, really don't mean to be rude when I do it, I promise. It’s just that... well, if I hear my coworkers working through a customer problem nearby, I kind of just want to help out, you know? So I might, um, jump in with the answer before they’ve completely finished talking, or... or even before anyone actually asked for my input. 

I just get so eager to solve the problem and help the customer. I hope that doesn't make me sound pushy or overbearing? I really just try to be a good team player. Is it okay that I do that sometimes, or is that the kind of thing you're looking for?
Do you often fidget, squirm, or feel unable to stay seated when you’re expected to sit still?

Well, I mean, I try my best to sit still, especially when I'm on the clock or in a meeting. I want to look professional, of course. But... I guess if you were really watching me, you might notice I'm not totally still. 

Like, even when I'm trying to look completely calm, my foot might be bouncing under the desk, or... or I might be clicking a pen during a meeting. And honestly, half the time I don't even realize I'm doing it until someone looks over! I really hope that doesn't make me seem unprofessional or anything. It's just a little nervous energy, I think. Does that make sense? I try to keep it out of sight as much as I can.
Have these restlessness or impulsive behaviors caused problems at work?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I really try my best to do a good job, and I love talking to the customers. People usually say I'm really friendly and helpful! But... well, lately, my supervisors have brought up a few things during my reviews. 

It's nothing terrible, I hope. They just mentioned that sometimes I leave a few customer tickets unfinished, or... or that I make some small mistakes that can kind of slow the rest of the team down. I really don't mean to, I promise. I'm trying so hard to keep up with everything and be a good employee. I just get a little ahead of myself sometimes, I think. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad worker? I really do get along great with the customers, and I always want to do what's best for the company. Is it okay that I'm struggling with that a little bit?
Do other people usually notice that you’re very fidgety or unable to stay still?

Well, um... I don't think so? I mean, I really try to be mindful of how I'm coming across, especially at work. I wouldn't want to be a distraction to anyone else. 

I guess maybe my wife might notice my foot tapping when we're watching TV or something, but... but I don't think people at work or out in public really see it. Like I said, I try to keep it under the desk or just, you know, small things. I really hope it's not something that stands out to people. Do you think that's something I need to be more worried about? I just want to make sure I'm presenting myself well.
Do you often have trouble keeping your attention on tasks, even when they are not boring?

Well, I... I'd like to think I'm a pretty good listener. I really do try to give things my full attention, especially when it's something important for work. 

But, um... I guess maybe sometimes, even if it's not a boring topic, I can struggle just a tiny bit? Like, when we have those longer coaching meetings with my supervisor, or if they hand out a new procedure to read through. I always start off doing great, completely focused! But then... after a few minutes, I'll suddenly realize my eyes have been moving across the page, or I've been looking at the person talking, but I didn't actually take in what was said. 

I always catch myself and try to get right back on track, though! I really hope that doesn't mean I'm being disrespectful or ignoring them. I definitely don't mean to. Is that... is that somewhat normal for people to do sometimes? I just want to make sure I'm doing my best.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder with prominent inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity symptoms beginning in childhood and causing occupational impairment. He reports chronic restlessness, fidgeting, difficulty sustaining attention, careless mistakes, talking out of turn/interrupting, and work problems with unfinished tasks and errors. No distinct episodes of elevated mood or increased energy were endorsed, and the presentation is predominantly inattentive rather than hyperkinetic/combined. This best fits F90.0.
